operations.title: Boundary-sum marks are four-node two-conic sections
operations.body: A boundary-sum mark forces one Delta coordinate to vanish, reducing the plane branch quartic to a binary quadratic in two squared differences; generically it factors into two conics meeting at four sign nodes. Single-edge marks miss all nodes. Four source terms have seven four-node marks; twenty-four have six plus one zero-node mark.

operations.title: Four-site source marked-section type census
operations.body: The checker classifies every mark in all 28 terms by exact node incidence, derives the representative binary-quadratic normal form, and verifies the two term profiles (0,7)x4 and (1,6)x24.

operations.title: Benincasa refines the four-site Gysin frontier to nodal two-conic sections
operations.body: Entry 1183 corrects the naive seven-E7 assembly. Boundary-sum marks force Delta_i=0, so their plane quartic is a binary quadratic in two squared differences: two conics meeting at four sign nodes. Single-edge marks avoid all nodes. Census: 4 terms have seven four-node marks; 24 terms have six plus one smooth mark. Next is the A1^4 root embedding inside resolved E7 and its primitive contraction/gluing with Entry 1181.

authority_basis.summary: Record the exact source marked-section classification for the four-site quartic double solid.
